To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
superdeformed configurations in S-32, and in neighboring odd-mass nuclei, are predicted within the Hartee-Fock approach with Skyrme interactions.
superdeformed bands with signature-split structure can be observed in 32S and neighboring nuclei.
superdeformed bands with a high angular momentum are possible in the S-32 nucleus and in its neighbors.
In summary, our research is concerned with
a detailed analysis of the properties of the superdeformed bands in the nuclei 32S, 33S, and 33Cl, as well as in the neighboring nuclei 31S, and 31 P.
the structure of superdeformed nuclei, and in particular with the superdeformed rotational states of the nuclei 32S and 31S.
a search for superdeformed configurations in the nuclei 32S, 33S, and 31S.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
superdeformed rotational configurations in 32 S and neighboring nuclei are predicted to exist and to be experimentally detectable.

, in the case of the superdeformed bands, the time-odd terms of the effective Skyrme interaction are essential for a correct description of the rotational properties of superdeformed bands in 32S and neighboring nuclei.
the superdeformed rotational band with I=10-18 in 32S has been identified and is the first example of a superdeformed rotational structure in a stable nucleus.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the superdeformed configurations in these nuclei are not very exotic and are expected to be easily accessible experimentally.

the superdeformed bands in the considered nuclei can be well described within the Hartree–Fock approach, with the SkyrMe interaction, if a proper account for the time-odd components of effective interaction is taken.

superdeformed rotational states are expected in 32S at excitation energies of about 20 MeV, in 33S and 31S at about 30 MeV, and in 31P and 33Cl at about 40 MeV, and that the superdeformed bands in 32S should be signature-split, while the bands in 31S and 33S should be signature-separated.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the superdeformed bands in 32S and neighboring nuclei can be populated in the fusion reaction, which is in contrast to the previous claims that the superdeformation cannot be observed in the fusion reaction.

the superdeformed bands are predicted to exist in a number of nuclei in the vicinity of 32S, with the excitation energy of the ground state of the superdeformed band ranging from 0.6 MeV in 33Cl to 1.6 MeV and 1.8 MeV in 31S and 31P respectively.
, in spite of the small size of the nuclei under study, the signature-separated bands are not necessarily the lowest in excitation energy.
